title: Count Ways to Choose Coprime Integers from Rows
summary: Given a m x n matrix mat filled with positive integers, determine the number of ways to select exactly one integer from each row such that the greatest common divisor of all selected integers is 1.
statement: Given a m x n matrix mat filled with positive integers, determine the number of ways to select exactly one integer from each row such that the greatest common divisor of all selected integers is 1. The result should be provided modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: mat has up to 150 rows and 150 columns, with values from one through 150.
Choose exactly one value from every row.
Count choices whose overall greatest common divisor is one, modulo 1,000,000,007.
hints: After processing some rows, only the gcd of the chosen values affects future choices.
Store the number of ways to reach each gcd and combine every state with every value in the next row.
Merge equal new gcds modulo the required modulus and finally read the gcd-one state.
The transition partitions all choices by their exact running gcd, so induction gives every complete selection once.
editorial: The transition partitions all choices by their exact running gcd, so induction gives every complete selection once.

tests.explanation: Three of the four row choices have greatest common divisor one.
Every selection has greatest common divisor two, so the answer is zero.
